question: On the already frozen R4 synthetic context generator, is an independently observable episode-start context sufficient to resolve the structural entity-0/entity-8 ambiguity without entity or family labels entering induction?
hypothesis: R4 context support alone induces eight classes with an entity-0/entity-8 collision. Adding only the first observed four-byte context as an episode boundary to each support signature yields nine clean three-member alias classes. A family-dependent rotation control removes cross-family alignment.

predecessor_evidence.nature: historical synthetic mechanism evidence; not independent unseen evaluation

arms.A0: R4 exact sorted support; no episode boundary
arms.A1: A0 exact support concatenated with the four context bytes emitted at context_index=0 for that entity-family stream; induction sees bytes only, not entity, family or context_index labels
arms.A2: A1 with family-specific cyclic rotation by (5*(family+1)) mod 16 before selection of the episode-boundary context; other data unchanged

frozen_design.sample_rule: For each of 9 entities and 3 families, reuse exactly R4's ordered context_index 0..15 bridge, one each, fixed byte formulas, unchanged R4 representation selection; no new corpus
frozen_design.split: No train/test split: deterministic mechanistic synthetic reuse only; no unseen/generalization claim
frozen_design.ordering: R4 emitter order for A0 and A1; frozen family rotation for A2
frozen_design.evaluator: Exact equality of canonical support signatures plus permitted observed phase four bytes; entity and family labels only in post-induction 36-pair audit

controls: A0 must reproduce R4's eight unique exact-support signatures and only collision pair (0,8) among nine entities.
Exactly 27 selected source surface motifs and 432 bridge records; each source has all sixteen contexts.
Induction cannot access entity/family IDs, generator context_index, transition labels, heldout samples or oracle corrections.
A2 modifies only boundary phase, not counts, context bytes, support or representation.
All three arms run before inspecting any primary outputs; no survivor selection or retuning.

classification_rules.supported: All validity and controls pass, A1 has exactly nine clean alias triplets with no collisions, and A2 loses at least one alias triplet.
classification_rules.mixed: All validity passes, A1 clean but A2 does not weaken alias alignment.
classification_rules.negative: All validity passes, A1 does not recover nine clean triplets.
classification_rules.invalid: Any source identity, A0 frozen replication, cardinality, induction-leakage, phase-change isolation, compute/capacity or deterministic-reproduction check fails.

interpretation_limits: Synthetic phase signal is introduced as an explicitly measured boundary; it is not an entity label in the inducer but is a strong synthetic information intervention. This establishes an observability dependency, NOT a learned language mechanism, natural-corpus transfer, or LLM-class competence.
